page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The fruit type
lines: The mango fruit is a drupe - a one-seeded
fleshy fruit with a hard, stony endocarp.
The coconut is also a drupe.
steps.why: Both fruits are the same TYPE (drupe); the question then asks what differs inside that same type - so name the type first.
common_mistakes: Writing that coconut is a nut. Botanically the coconut is a drupe with a fibrous mesocarp.
steps.memory_tip: Drupe = stone fruit; mango and coconut both carry a stony endocarp.
steps.margin_note: Name drupe and say it covers both fruits before differentiating.

steps.why: The difference lives in ONE layer, the mesocarp - fleshy in mango, fibrous in coconut - and in which part is eaten.
common_mistakes: Calling the white kernel of coconut the mesocarp. The kernel is the endosperm; the fibre (coir) is the mesocarp.
steps.memory_tip: In mango you eat the middle wall; in coconut you eat the seed's endosperm.
steps.margin_note: Mesocarp is the key word on both sides of the contrast.
